reason: The multi-provider client library is replaced by harness-owned drivers for the four provider wire protocols on net/http, with the model catalogue kept as harness data, because every piece of debt the library carries comes from it standing between the harness and the wire.

No upstream source imports it; it is declared only because the OAR library embedded in subagent-oar depends on it for an in-process Pi runtime that upstream does not test. The Go host links no coding agent as a library; an outside agent is a separate process.
Its one job, framing a server-sent-events response body into events for the DeepSeek adapter, is done by a small reader written in the harness on bufio and shared by every provider driver.

It exists only because of npm: the Claude Agent SDK names it as a peer dependency, so the consuming package must declare it, and no upstream source file imports it. Go modules have no peer dependencies.

The patch stops the library re-parsing accumulated tool arguments on every fragment and keeps a Gemini tool-call signature the library dropped. The Go harness owns the stream decoder, so fragments are forwarded unparsed and unknown provider fields are kept as raw JSON; there is no third-party file to patch.

The entry denies an npm install script, which pnpm requires to be reviewed. Go never runs module code when it downloads a module, and the package is not in the Go design because no multi-provider library pulls it in.
The entry denies an npm install script of a dependency of the Google SDK that pi-ai pulls in. Go has no install scripts, and the package is not in the Go design.

The supply-chain waiting period is switched off for this library because its releases carry the model catalogue. In Go the catalogue is a data file owned by the harness, so learning about a new model never requires taking new third-party code the day it is published.
The package is exempted only because pi-ai depends on it and is itself exempted. Without the library in the request path, its dependencies are not part of the Go build.

title: The pi-ai adapter is tied to one library version by drift gates, a generated provider-metadata file with its own commit and CI check, and a hand-changed digest seed

reason: The option lists, provider metadata and serialized request become the harness's own code and data, so there is no outside library to drift from, and the request-prefix digest is computed over the bytes actually sent.

title: Three runtime dependencies are declared by packages whose source never imports them (pi-ai and pi-coding-agent in subagent-oar, @anthropic-ai/sdk in subagent-claude-code)

reason: Both causes are npm rules: a package that embeds a library must re-declare what the bundle leaves outside, and a consumer must supply peer packages. A Go module requires only the packages its code imports, and go mod tidy removes the rest.

title: Model-provider wire drivers and model catalogue (replaces the pi-ai family)

The model catalogue is data owned by the harness, not a code dependency
Vendor modules are allowed for vendor authentication only, in separate provider components
No coding agent is linked into the host as a library
Four routes, one per protocol; a config change does not affect a running stream; credential rules
Tool-argument fragments pass through byte for byte in linear time
Stream order, truncated streams and disjoint token counts for every protocol
Replay metadata, including unknown provider fields, survives a round trip; a changed prefix drops signed reasoning
One HTTP attempt per call; failures keep status, retry delay, request id and cause
Cancellation closes the connection; idle timeout counts keep-alive bytes
Attribution header wins, redirects are refused, proxy policy applies
One conformance table over all protocol drivers, including unsupported options and deviation switches
Embedded catalogue validates and resolves in layers; unlisted models are still accepted
A provider with its own authentication step plugs in without changing drivers or transport
Server-sent-events reader for provider response streams (replaces eventsource-parser)
SSE framing table: line endings, multi-line data, byte-order mark, comments, byte-at-a-time input
